cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The shared virtualenv editable installation resolved workbench to a stale v1.8.6 worktree, so the formal CLI failed during import before dispatch.
impact: The first formal append/help attempt did not reach the line event writer.
lesson: Run formal CLI commands with the current worktree backend explicitly first on PYTHONPATH.

cause: The existing numeric producer keys recipe, artifact and child paths only by the step fingerprint, so a second real source binding is rejected as an occupied recipe path before it can publish a distinct node.
impact: The minimum host/evidence-port RED probe cannot execute the same transform against two source bindings without identity collision.
lesson: Bind every dataset producer identity to the resolved lineage source artifact, node and content hash before writing paths or index entries.

cause: A read-only process-control status query used an unsupported subcommand; devline_control.py exposes verify and index rather than status.
impact: No product or formal state was changed; the valid verify/index commands remain available.
lesson: Use only the documented devline_control subcommands when inspecting formal line state.

cause: The documented index --all inspection command stopped on an existing frozen Context Pack drift before producing an index.
impact: The inspection did not change product or formal state; full-line status must be read from the line manifests/events or a context-refresh procedure authorized by the formal process.
lesson: Run index only against a context-consistent formal root, and treat Context Pack drift as a stop condition rather than bypassing it.

cause: The derived-output identity implementation now binds numeric, prepared-data and workflow-capability dataset paths, artifact ids, graph children and node-index entries to resolved input lineage while retaining conflict fail-closed behavior.
